resources.name: Michigan State University Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS)
resources.hours: Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; crisis counselors 24/7 by pressing 1
resources.description: Counseling and crisis support for MSU students, in person and virtual. Ongoing services are not available to students living outside Michigan.
resources.notes: Old address caps.msu.edu redirects here. Cost and languages not stated on the page. Eligibility stated only as students; ongoing care not offered to students residing outside Michigan. After-hours: call 517-355-8270 and press 1.

resources.name: University of Michigan Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS)
resources.hours: Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. (5 p.m. in spring/summer); Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
resources.description: Counseling and psychological services through University Health Service for University of Michigan Ann Arbor students, at the Michigan Union.
resources.notes: caps.umich.edu redirects to uhc.umich.edu. No CAPS-specific after-hours number is listed; the page lists 911, 988 and U-M Psychiatric Emergency Service 734-936-5900. Cost: page says the vast majority of UHC services are free for students and not billed to insurance, but does not state CAPS cost specifically. Eligibility and languages not explicitly stated for CAPS. Hours: Friday figure and spring/summer detail taken from a second fetch of the same site; confirm before publishing.

resources.name: University of Michigan-Dearborn Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS)
resources.hours: Office Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Friday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; after hours, weekends and closures call and press 2 for a licensed clinician
resources.description: Free counseling for current University of Michigan-Dearborn students, in person or remote, with after-hours phone access to a licensed clinician.
resources.notes: Page states appointments only for current UM-Dearborn students. Languages not stated. A 2024 faculty handbook page (not checked directly) lists a different crisis number, so use only the number on the CAPS page.

resources.name: Wayne State University Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS)
resources.hours: Office Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.; at all other times and during closures call 313-577-CAPS (2277)
resources.description: Counseling and a free mental health assessment for currently enrolled Wayne State students, with a 24-hour phone line outside office hours.
resources.notes: After-hours number 313-577-2277 (313-577-CAPS). Page says the initial assessment is free; cost of ongoing counseling not stated, so cost left blank. Languages not stated.

resources.name: University of Detroit Mercy Wellness Center Personal Counseling
resources.description: Personal counseling with Michigan-licensed clinicians for University of Detroit Mercy students, requested through an online contact form or email.
resources.notes: No counseling phone is listed on the counseling page; 313-993-1185 on the Wellness Center page is the Health Clinic line, so phone left blank. Contact: personalcounselingwc@udmercy.edu. Hours differ between pages (8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. fall/winter on counseling page; 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Wellness Center page), so hours left blank. Counseling page says 'no charge' for students; Wellness Center page lists accepted insurers, so confirm. For after-hours emergencies the pages list 911 and 988. Counseling page still cites an old lifeline number; do not copy it.

resources.name: Michigan Crisis and Access Line (MiCAL) and 988
resources.description: Free, confidential crisis counseling by call or text for anyone in Michigan in emotional distress, a mental health or substance use crisis, or worried about someone.
resources.notes: MiCAL answers most Michigan 988 calls; seven counties have regional 988 centers with MiCAL as backup. Languages not confirmed on the page. MiCAL site is a JavaScript portal; phone and hours confirmed on michigan.gov.

resources.name: Michigan 211
resources.description: Free, confidential referrals to local help such as food, housing, bills and crisis support, by phone, text or chat. Open to anyone in Michigan.
resources.notes: Referral service, not a clinical crisis line. Text and data rates may apply.

resources.name: Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network (DWIHN) Crisis and Support Line
resources.description: Free, confidential 24/7 crisis and support line for anyone in Wayne County facing a mental health or substance use emergency, with mobile crisis and walk-in options.
resources.notes: Mobile Crisis 844-462-7474 also listed. The text option is the national Crisis Text Line as shown on DWIHN's page. Website offered in English, Spanish and Arabic; phone line languages not stated.

resources.name: Washtenaw County Community Mental Health Crisis Services
resources.description: Round-the-clock phone crisis line, mobile crisis team and suicide risk assessments for Washtenaw County residents with urgent needs.
resources.notes: Page says crisis services are for urgent needs that could cause harm within 48 hours. Cost and languages not stated on the page. Another state listing shows 734-996-4747; not used.

resources.name: Oakland Community Health Network (OCHN) Crisis Line
resources.description: Crisis line for anyone in Oakland County in a suicidal, mental health or substance use crisis, with a separate mobile crisis unit for adults.
resources.notes: Non-crisis Access line (248) 464-6363, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Site offers English, Spanish and Arabic; phone languages not stated. Common Ground, previously the crisis provider, now lists its own number (see separate entry); a Common Ground press release dated 2026-01-29 says OCHN defunding forced it to transfer adult crisis care. Confirm which number is current for Oakland adults.

resources.name: Common Ground Crisis Hub
resources.description: Free, confidential crisis support, 24/7 by phone, with text and chat through 988, for anyone seeking crisis help, run by a Michigan crisis agency.
resources.notes: Added entry. Common Ground staffs MiCAL under state contract. Homepage shows 'Crisis Hub 1-800-231-1127', 'Text 988' and 'free, confidential crisis support 24/7'. Service area on the Oakland page not independently confirmed; area set to Oakland County because that is its home base, check before publishing.

resources.name: Macomb County Community Mental Health (MCCMH) Crisis Line
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
resources.description: Crisis line answered day and night for Macomb County residents in a mental health crisis, run by Macomb County Community Mental Health.
resources.notes: Non-crisis access: 855-996-2264 or 586-948-0222, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Cost and languages for the crisis line not stated.

resources.name: Community Mental Health Authority of Clinton, Eaton and Ingham Counties (CMHA-CEI) Crisis Services
resources.description: 24/7 crisis triage, evaluation and screening for psychiatric emergencies for residents of Clinton, Eaton and Ingham counties, including the East Lansing area.
resources.notes: Ingham County's crisis services are run by CMHA-CEI, not the county health department. Local number 517-346-8460; TTY 7-1-1; non-emergency 888-800-1559. Cost and languages not stated. A Crisis Care Center is listed as 'coming soon'.

resources.name: MY Mental Wellness Helpline (Islamic Center of Detroit)
resources.hours: Monday to Friday, 6 p.m. to 10 p.m.
resources.description: Free, anonymous after-hours peer listening line with faith-informed, culturally sensitive responders, run through Naseeha. Not a therapy or crisis line.
resources.notes: Page says it is not 24/7 and not a crisis service; for crisis call 988, for emergencies 911. Outside hours it points to 1-866-NASEEHA. Languages not stated.

resources.name: MY Mental Wellness Clinic (Islamic Center of Detroit)
resources.hours: Monday to Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.
resources.description: Free, faith-based and culturally guided therapy with licensed clinicians for children, teens, adults and elders, in person at the Islamic Center of Detroit or virtually.
resources.notes: Phone left blank because the site shows two different numbers: (313) 781-3479 (appointments, call or text) and (313) 584-4143 (main clinic on the homepage). Confirm before publishing. Homepage states care is free. Address 14350 Tireman Ave., Detroit, MI 48228. Languages not stated.

resources.name: Michigan Muslim Mental Health Directory (The Family & Youth Institute)
resources.description: Directory of Muslim mental health professionals in Southeastern Michigan, with plain-language descriptions of provider types. Listings are informational and not endorsed.
resources.notes: No phone or hours; individual listings were not audited. The FYI says it does not endorse listed therapists. Page text refers to Southeastern Michigan, so area may be better labelled Southeast Michigan.

resources.name: ICNA Relief Michigan Muslim Family Services Counseling
resources.description: Licensed counseling and telehealth for individuals and families of all backgrounds, in a culturally appropriate setting that includes Islamic counseling, by appointment.
resources.notes: Muslim Family Services (MFS) is the ICNA Relief Michigan counseling program; the domain muslimfamilyservices.org now shows unrelated gambling spam and was not used. Office 12500 Mitchell St, Detroit. Hours differ between the page body and footer, so hours left blank. Cost not stated on the official site.

resources.name: Cognitive Care Center
resources.area: Southeast Michigan (Novi, Canton, Ann Arbor, Inkster)
resources.hours: Monday to Saturday 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.; Sunday by appointment
resources.description: Outpatient therapy, assessments and groups for children, teens and adults, at four Southeast Michigan locations. Accepts most major insurance plans.
resources.notes: Not described on its own site as Muslim-specific; site mentions cultural diversity and sensitivity. Hours taken from Contact page; homepage says Monday to Saturday. Insurances listed on payments page; Medicaid and Medicare accepted. Support groups $50 per person. Contact page lists a personal Gmail among emails.

resources.name: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS) Behavioral Health
resources.description: Counseling, psychiatric services, case management and peer support for adults, children and families in Southeast Michigan, including Arab American and immigrant communities.
resources.notes: 1-833-774-0002 is labeled 'Customer Service Hotline' on the page, not a crisis or intake line. Page lists a sliding fee scale policy and DWIHN 24-hour helpline 1-800-241-4949; cost left blank. Hours not stated. Site blocks automated fetches; read via browser.

resources.name: Arab-American and Chaldean Council (ACC) Behavioral Health Program
resources.area: Southeast Michigan (Oakland, Macomb and Wayne counties)
resources.description: CARF-accredited outpatient counseling and mental health services for individuals, families and children at five culturally sensitive centers in Oakland, Macomb and Wayne counties.
resources.notes: Phone is the organization's main Troy number from the site footer; the behavioral health page also shows 800-603-7118 without a clear label, so confirm the program's own intake line. The site's HTML contains hidden spam text (unrelated drug terms), so it may have been tampered with; page content on the program looks genuine. Cost, hours, languages not stated.

resources.name: Chaldean Community Foundation Project Light
resources.description: Mental health screening, consultation and therapy from licensed trilingual therapists for Michigan residents aged 13 and up, regardless of insurance status.
resources.notes: Cost: page says services are provided regardless of insurance status, which does not mean free; cost field is therefore blank in effect, recheck. Also provides mental health referrals for refugees in Southeast Michigan. Hours for the program not stated; main lobby hours differ by day.

dropped.name: Muslim Family Services Detroit (muslimfamilyservices.org)
dropped.reason: That domain now shows unrelated gambling spam. The real Muslim Family Services is ICNA Relief Michigan's counseling program, which is included as its own entry.

dropped.name: Zaman International
dropped.reason: Official site (zamaninternational.org) describes poverty relief, a case management program and a health center, but I found no mental health or counseling support, so it is excluded.

dropped.name: Samaritas refugee mental health
dropped.reason: Could not confirm a specific refugee mental health service, phone or eligibility on an official Samaritas page (the refugee-services URL returned 404). Only secondary sources mention it.

dropped.name: Bethany Christian Services refugee mental health
dropped.reason: Official site blocked automated access (403) and no mental health service could be confirmed.

dropped.name: Michigan Peer Warmline (MiCAL)
dropped.reason: Added candidate not kept. Official MiCAL page describes it but the page text shows no phone or hours; the number appeared only in a search summary.
